_comment: Pre-registered hook-latency budget (road-to-credible-install Phase 1). Committed BEFORE the first optimization landed, per the roadmap's pre-registration discipline: the numbers below are the acceptance bar the precompile + single-process work is measured against, not a post-hoc fit. Consumed by the bench harness (scripts/bench_hook_latency) and its CI gate. Every budget carries an owner and a review date per the Phase-6 budget-ownership lint.

hardware_reference.ci: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner (the numbers the gate enforces)
hardware_reference.floor: 1 vCPU reference container (documented ceiling, not CI-enforced)

gate_remeasure._comment: OFF (attempts 1 = measure once, no re-measure). The mechanism exists in bench_hook_latency.ts: under --gate a slot over its cap is re-measured and the MINIMUM p95 kept, because a load spike inside one 50-run sample moves p95 up and never down. It ships DISABLED because pre_tool_use_cap_derivation.why_not_a_retry_or_best_of_n rejected it as the first move on measured grounds — the spread is between runner CLASSES (p50 111-148 ms), not noise within one machine, so a slow runner measures slow twice. Two CI runs of the mechanism agree: it recovered 151->150 and 160->153, i.e. 1-7 ms against a 42 ms spread. Set attempts to 3 ONLY as the escalation that same block names, if the re-derived 175 cap starts flapping.

normalized.control: node -e 0, measured through the identical spawnSync harness in the same run
normalized._comment: Observe-only measurement row, printed on every bench run and gating nothing. Every slot reading is spawn + interpreter start + bundle load + concern work, and only the last term is ours; the control isolates the process-spawn term so excess_ms = slot - control is closer to this tree's own cost than the raw reading. It exists to collect the data a future normalized gate would need, and to sharpen pre_tool_use_cap_derivation.revisit_if — which currently reads runner speed off the p50, a cheaper signal that needs no extra measurement. Arming this row would be a config change (p95_excess_ci + observe_only false), and the limitation below says why that is not justified today.
normalized._measured_limitation_2026_08_19: THE CONTROL UNDER-CORRECTS, measured, and this is recorded so nobody arms the row believing a property that was not shown. Same commit, two environments: darwin read slot 101 / control 45 / excess 56 ms; GitHub ubuntu read slot 151 / control 26 / excess 124 ms. The control went DOWN while the slot went UP, because node -e 0 covers interpreter startup only while a dispatch also loads a ~1 MB bundle and runs the concern chain — the dominant and varying term. So excess_ms is NOT portable across hardware classes. Whether it is nonetheless steadier than the absolute WITHIN one runner class is UNMEASURED: two CI runs read control 26/28 ms and excess 124/125 ms against raw first samples of 151/160, which is suggestive but n=2 and computed on post-re-measure values. Collect from the nightly before setting a bar, and keep the row observe-only if it does not hold rather than arming a second flapping gate.

pre_tool_use_cap_derivation._comment: Why p95_ci is 175 and not the 150 registered on 2026-07-27. 150 was NOT bent around a red check — it was measured to sit INSIDE the legitimate distribution, which concern-activation-policy.md § Deriving a threshold names as a false-positive generator by construction: `a threshold inside the legitimate distribution`. The gate was flapping on IDENTICAL code, and the flap was already diagnosed in this tree by road-to-per-turn-hook-economy step 0.5 — it names three main runs at 151, 152 and 117 ms and concludes cross-runner variance after step 0.4 excluded the CLI wrapper (2 ms). What was missing was never the diagnosis; it was moving the cap.
pre_tool_use_cap_derivation.rule_cited: concern-activation-policy.md § Deriving a threshold — 'the observed legitimate distribution's 99th percentile, plus one'. The load-bearing half is 'outside the distribution'; a threshold inside it is a false-positive generator by construction.
pre_tool_use_cap_derivation.rule_applied: max + ~11%, i.e. 175 — NOT p99+1, and the substitution is deliberate rather than a slip. Over this sample p99+1 is 158 ms, which sits ONE millisecond above the observed max: that satisfies the rule's letter while leaving no room for a tail measured on 10 of 33 runs. The '+1' in the cited rule is calibrated to a shadow window that emits `would_fire` at several candidate thresholds and therefore knows its own distribution densely; this sample is 10 single points from CI logs and does not. Where the rule's precision assumption does not hold, the honest move is more headroom and a stated departure, not a number that borrows an authority it does not have.
pre_tool_use_cap_derivation.measured_failure_rate: 5 of 33 tests.yml runs on main (15%) failed this step, 2026-08-16..18. Several of those runs carry a failure followed by a success for the SAME step, i.e. the standing workaround was re-running the job by hand.

observed_p95_ms_gated_cli_leg._comment: One value per run, pre_tool_use, the `via cli` leg the gate actually compares. Every one is legitimate code — the reds differ from the greens only in which runner drew the job. SELECTION RULE, stated because it bounds the derivation: these 10 are the runs whose Static Checks log was read, not a sample designed for coverage — 6 greens and 4 reds picked from the head of the 33-run window, plus this branch's own PR run. The 5th red main run's value was never captured, so the true max over all 33 runs is UNRECORDED and may exceed 157 ms. That is the main reason the applied formula carries more headroom than p99+1.
observed_p95_ms_gated_cli_leg.spread: 115-157 ms, i.e. 42 ms of run-to-run variance on unchanged code — 24% of the new 175 ms cap and 28% of the old 150 ms one

pre_tool_use_cap_derivation.why_not_a_retry_or_best_of_n: A second bench on the same job would not help: the spread is between runner classes (p50 111-148 ms), not transient noise within one machine, so a slow runner measures slow twice. Retry logic is the escalation if 175 flaps, not the first move.
pre_tool_use_cap_derivation.revisit_if: The p50 — not the p95 — of a green run rises above 160 ms. Read the MEDIAN because that is the runner-speed indicator: the observed p50 range is 111-148 ms, so a p50 past 160 is outside every machine this window saw and is the cost itself growing. It then belongs to the owning roadmap (road-to-per-turn-hook-economy, D-2: the dispatcher's own payload read+parse, once per event) rather than to a third cap raise. Raising this number again without a measured distribution beside it is the config-bending this block exists to make visible.
pre_tool_use_cap_derivation._revisit_if_correction: First written as 'a green run measures p95 above 160 ms', which round 2 finding 9 refuted from inside this same block: 160 sits 15 ms BELOW the new cap and 3 ms above the observed max, so the very first green 161 ms run would pass the gate and simultaneously trip a trigger declaring the variance to be over. A trigger has to live outside the spread its own cap absorbs, and on a p95 with 42 ms of runner spread no such point exists below 175. The p50 has a spread of 37 ms and a ceiling of 148, so it does.

per_turn_composite._comment: D-1 of road-to-per-turn-hook-economy: the slot budgets above gate per EVENT, and a single tool call fires both pre_tool_use and post_tool_use with their full concern chains. A ten-tool-call turn therefore pays twenty dispatcher cold starts plus the prompt and stop slots while every individual slot stays green — the number the user experiences has no row. This row is that number. Registered by step 4.1; the CEILING is step 4.2 and is the maintainer's, so the row ships observe-only and CANNOT fail a build. Definition before bar, deliberately: two people computing two different composites would both call the row green.
per_turn_composite._aggregation_note: Documentation of the code, not an input to it: the bench reads tool_calls from this file but hardcodes the p50 aggregation and re-implements the formula, so editing `aggregation` or `definition` changes nothing. Kept because a row whose meaning lives only in a TS file is unreadable here; corrected from silence to a stated non-binding after the R2 review flagged both keys as unread.
per_turn_composite.observe_only_decision: b-per-turn-composite-bar option (b) — council 2026-08-20, 2/2 quorum, both seats convergent: "mark (pre + post) x 10 + ups + stop observe-only for one release, then derive an absolute ceiling and a pathology net from that distribution." Option (a), adopting the source draft's p50 <= 1.5 s, was refused because no run in this tree produced that number and an invented bar on a summed metric is the flappiest gate available. Option (c), declining the composite, was refused because it leaves D-1 permanently unmeasurable, which is the defect itself.
per_turn_composite.observe_only_extended: EXTENDED 2026-08-23 - b-composite-ceiling-value option (c), AI council 2026-08-23, 2/2 quorum (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 + openai/codex-default), convergent across two passes. Option (b) (a p50-derived cap plus a separate pathology threshold) was chosen first and then found NOT EXECUTABLE: its own Resolved-when requires the row to carry "the number with the n and session count it was derived from", and check_composite_arming reports n = 0 - no store at agents/evidence/hook-composite-readings.jsonl at all. Arming from local bench runs was considered and refused: the predicate would have accepted them, because composeReadingRecord gives each local invocation its own session id by design, but every local session is ONE machine and that is exactly the under-sampling MIN_SESSIONS = 2 was written to exclude. Satisfying a counter while defeating its purpose is the silent-green the arming procedure exists to prevent. So p50_ci stays null and observe_only stays true. REOPENS when check_composite_arming reports armable (>= 10 readings from >= 2 distinct CI runner sessions), at which point the blocker is answered again with a number in hand. Nothing about arming_procedure, arming_precondition or the 2026-08-20 decision is weakened here - only the date at which a number is chosen moves.
per_turn_composite.arming_procedure: 1. Collect the printed composite from every CI gate run across one release cycle — the bench prints it on every run, gated or not. 2. Set p50_ci to an ABSOLUTE cap derived from that distribution, never a creep window: shared CI runners flap, which is why regression_gate.max_regression_pct is already 200. 3. Keep the pathology net separate from the cap, so one spike is caught as a pathology rather than by lowering the cap. 4. Set observe_only to false — no code change is needed to arm it.
per_turn_composite.arming_precondition: At least 10 CI gate readings of the composite, from at least 2 distinct runner sessions. Below that the estimator cannot separate code cost from runner load: the transport-isolation cell added for b-payload-read-parse-dominates read 44-157% at n=12 and 69-74% at n=50 on ONE machine, and a bar set from single-digit readings would carry that same instability.
per_turn_composite._arming_precondition_honesty: The 10-readings / 2-sessions floor is a STATED MINIMUM, not a derived one — it is the point below which the n=12 instability above was directly observed on a sibling metric in this same roadmap. Revisit-if: a release cycle produces the readings and their spread demands a wider floor, or the composite turns out to be dominated by one slot, in which case that slot's own cap is the better gate and this row stays observe-only permanently with that recorded.
per_turn_composite._observe_only_note: While observe_only is true the bench PRINTS the composite on every run, including the CI gate run, and never fails on it. Setting p50_ci to a number and observe_only to false is the whole of step 4.2 — no code change is needed to arm it. Do not arm it from a single run: the composite sums four slot measurements and multiplies two of them by tool_calls, so it accumulates runner variance faster than any single slot (risk 5), which is why the same absolute-cap-plus-pathology-net posture the slots use applies here too.

regression_gate._comment: Pathology net only — the ABSOLUTE budgets above are the binding gate for wall-clock. The original 20% window was falsified by measured GitHub-runner variance: two CI runs of IDENTICAL code measured p95 77-89 ms and 92-103 ms (+23% run-to-run, 2026-07-27, runs 30303438480 / round-2 tests.yml). Same rationale as the regression_pct 200 override on the evaluator timing budgets: a tight creep rule on shared-runner wall-clock flaps; sizes/counts keep tight windows, timings get absolute caps.

honest_null_consequence: If the budget is missed after precompile + single-process + lazy I/O, hooks ship default-off with an explicit opt-in flag and the measured numbers published under a 'known cost' heading. A resident-dispatcher daemon is NOT improvised as a rescue (council 2026-07-26).
